blocks.title: Pattern Recipe
blocks.text: IIFE + closure + returned object = ==private state== and exactly **one** public name.

items: import/export gives the same privacy at file level
Statically analyzable and tree-shakeable — prefer it
An imported name is a live view of the exporter's binding
Closer to closure capture than to assignment

lines: } // no way to set balance directly
const multiplier = n => x => x * n;
const double = multiplier(2); // closes over n
const add = a => b => a + b;
const cache = new Map(); // lives in closure

items: Debounce: the closure holds the pending timeoutId
So a new call can clear the previous timer
Throttle: the closure holds a lastRun timestamp
React: a stale closure is an old render's captured state
The deps array decides which closure stays live
`map` + addEventListener: each handler holds its own item
A cursor variable gives `next()` with no generator syntax
A `.then` callback still sees the starting function's vars
A closure keeps its whole captured record alive
Collected only when every closure on it is unreachable
Lifetime belongs to the function, not to the call
A detached node pins its entire subtree, not just itself
Removal from the document is not enough on its own
WeakMap holds keys weakly; the entry dies with the key
The right tool for caches attached to objects
WeakRef when you need one droppable handle
Two closures from one call share one environment
A tiny surviving closure can pin a huge sibling capture
Mitigate with `bigData = null` when you are done
Or capture the big value in a narrower inner scope
Lookup cost grows with chain depth; engines cache and inline
Rarely the bottleneck — measure before restructuring
A closure built in a hot loop allocates per iteration
Hoist it out if it captures nothing loop-specific
`eval` and `with` defeat static scope analysis
The whole enclosing function goes slow-path
DevTools heap snapshot: Retainers shows the holding closure

caption.text: Part 3 of JS CLOSURES & SCOPE. Every JavaScript bug that starts with "but it logged 3 three times" is the same bug: closures capture bindings, not values. These 10 pages are the full field notes — scope chains, the var/let/const table, the two-phase hoisting model, the TDZ error messages decoded, the loop capture problem with all three fixes, IIFEs, the module pattern, and the leak patterns that follow closures around. Save it for the next time an error says "Cannot access 'x' before initialization" and you know exactly what to check.
